title: fix(polli-cli): exit via exitCode/ExitSignal instead of process.exit (wrong exit code + libuv abort on Windows)
author: rekty
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary

Fixes #15535 — on Windows with Node >= 23, every `polli` error path that called `process.exit(1)` after a `fetch` round-trip aborted libuv (`Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING)`, upstream nodejs/node#56645) and the shell observed exit code **127 instead of 1**. Scripts and CI jobs checking the exit status got garbage.

Root cause: `process.exit()` while undici's keep-alive sockets are still open trips the libuv assertion on Windows (Node 23.x+); because the abort happens inside `process.exit(1)`, the intended exit code is lost.

## Changes

- Add an `ExitSignal` error class in `lib/output.ts`; `fail()` and `exitWithError()` now throw it instead of calling `process.exit(1)`.
- The top-level `parseAsync().catch()` in `src/index.ts` converts `ExitSignal` to `process.exitCode = n` and returns, so the event loop unwinds cleanly (sockets close, then the process exits with the right code).
- All 26 inline `process.exit(1)` call sites in commands now `throw new ExitSignal(1)`.
- `gen chat` readline paths (`/exit`, close handler, fatal budget hint) set `process.exitCode` directly — throwing there would only produce an unhandled rejection.
- `docs.ts` rethrows `ExitSignal` from its local `catch` so the error is not double-reported by the surrounding `fail()`.

## Verification (Windows 11, Node v24.18.0)

| Command | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `polli docs /nope` | assertion + exit **127** | exit **1**, no assertion |
| `polli gen image "test" --width 0` | assertion + exit **127** | exit **1**, no assertion |
| `polli gen transcribe missing.mp3` | assertion + exit **127** | exit **1**, no assertion |
| `polli models --type bogus` | exit 1 (no I/O) | exit **1** |
| `polli models --type embedding` | exit 0 | exit **0** |

Minimal repro from the issue (`node -e "fetch(...).then(...); process.exit(1)"`) still aborts — this is a Node runtime bug — but the CLI no longer calls `process.exit()` on any code path, so it is unaffected.

gist.headline: Exit one, not 127
gist.blurb: Polli CLI errors now leave quietly and return the exit code scripts expect. Windows and Node had been making quite a production of it.
gist.summary: Polli CLI replaces process.exit(1) with ExitSignal and process.exitCode, so error paths after a fetch exit with code 1 instead of triggering a libuv assertion and returning 127 on Windows with Node 23+.
gist.impact: Windows scripts and CI jobs can reliably detect Polli CLI failures by exit code 1, without the libuv abort; successful commands still return 0.
